scope: One disposable Kind v1.36.1 cluster. A small server-side dry-run Pod request is compared before and after a namespace CPU/memory ResourceQuota; a second request at the remaining declared budget is admitted. Two case-owned PriorityClasses are read back and resolved onto dry-run Pods, with preemption disabled. One tokenless, low-resource HTTP fixture Pod is observed Ready and read through the Kubernetes API Service proxy before and after quota checks, and looks up the exact in-cluster Kubernetes Service via CoreDNS. This does not create pressure or simulate training. It does not demonstrate actual scheduler ordering under contention, protection of built-in control-plane components, CoreDNS resolution latency, real metrics scrape success, log forwarding lag, node/network capacity, or production service availability.

checks.claim: Case-owned priority metadata declares shared service above training, without preemption
Without a namespace quota, the small synthetic training request reaches admission
before quota enforcement: the steady fixture serves its marker and resolves the exact in-cluster Service
The namespace quota readback matches the fixed small budget
Quota usage readback accounts for only the steady fixture before probes
ResourceQuota refuses a request that exceeds the declared CPU budget
The named quota separately refuses an over-budget memory request
The request at the remaining declared budget is admitted with resolved low non-preempting priority
after quota refusal and bounded admission probes: the steady fixture serves its marker and resolves the exact in-cluster Service
The same healthy Pod remains and the dry-run requests created no training Pods
The steady fixture resolves to the higher declared shared-service priority
